correctness.rationale: Definitions and quantifiers cover any finite forest including isolates and empty graph. Easy direction extends any selection of one endpoint per induced-matching edge to an MIS. Reverse direction is induction on vertices: isolated outsiders can be deleted; a leaf inside S forces its neighbor when labeled zero and yields an induced-matching edge with residual outside N[u]; a leaf outside S whose neighbor is in S uses the fixed-positive u branch and again recurses outside N[u]; an outside leaf with neighbor outside S can be deleted without changing MIS trace patterns. Every case preserves actual shattering and the induced-matching property. The C5 obstruction is explicitly verified. The standalone checker independently compares traces against induced-matchings in all 3272 labeled forests of orders 0..6; these finite checks do not substitute for induction.

evidence: Liu et al., SoCG 2024, Lemma 27, states VCdim(M(G)) <= nu_bi(G) for every graph, where nu_bi is bipartite induced-matching number.
The same paper explicitly distinguishes ordinary induced matchings by requiring both endpoint sides to be independent. In P4, nu_bi(P4)=2 and nu_ind(P4)=VCdim(M(P4))=1.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected same-object primary statement is the 2024 general inequality VCdim(M(G)) <= nu_bi(G). Its bipartite induced matching parameter is strictly larger than the ordinary induced matching parameter even on P4; thus it does not imply the forest-wide if-and-only-if support theorem. Earlier works on induced matching constructions or MIS enumeration give the lower direction only. Direct semantic searches of indexed mathematical findings and available historical claims did not identify stronger coverage. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of global historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The question has a natural model-theoretic/learning meaning: which finite sets of vertex membership statements can vary independently across maximal independent solutions? The exact support criterion answers more than the numerical dimension for the entire forest class and identifies the classical induced matching as the governing parameter. It also precisely locates an acyclic/cyclic boundary, illustrated by C5. The 2024 published general matching bound leaves a genuine gap on P4 even within forests, making the exact improvement nontrivial rather than a parameter renaming.
